title: Tony Jackson, Tom Anderson's, and cousin Louis Prevost with Louis Armstrong
summary: He never heard Tony Jackson; he describes Tom Anderson's place, where his cousin Louis Prevost sat in with Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Somebody told me that Tony Jackson, the piano player and singer played there. Did you ever hear Tony Jackson? I think he left here when you were very young. I thought you might have heard him.

No, I used to know, I knew where he was living at though. He was living around there, right around the corner from there, what I'm talking about. He was living on the corner I think. Corner in Hillary.
Did you ever hear another fellow, Alfred Wilson, a piano player in the district on Basin Street there? It was way back maybe around 1910 to 15 along that period.
Well, Alfred, Alfred William, he was playing with a violin player and a bass and a guitar at that time. Right on the corner, let's see now.
That was a different man I think. This was.
Right. Benville Street. He was playing Benville and Basin. It had a tile front there, that's all gone.
Was that Tom Anderson's place or?
He had a saloon on Iberville and Basin though too I think. I think they had a trio sometimes, string trio with guitar and bass and there.
Yeah, but I don't, I can't think of it. That was Frank Woerley. That was Frank Woerley too. Had that place. That's my knowing as far as I've been.
Frank Woerley had that place too. And Tom Anderson was on Basin Street on Ramport Street.
I know he had just down for the Tencent Storys, I think he had one place.

Yeah, that's where he had a place. Yeah, a big place because Louis, my cousin was Louis Prevost, you know. Oh yeah. He used to play a clarinet and then he was playing with a lyric, playing trumpet. But I used to go sit up there and sit up there with him and eat and drink up there when, at Tom Anderson when Louis Armstrong was playing up there. Cause he used to come bring his cornet. My cousin used to put the clarinet in his pocket. Two pieces in there. Two pieces in each pocket and go up there and play. And I used to go up there with him, he used to go up there every night. Cause he was living with me then, rooming on St. Claude and Dumaine. Still and still there, yeah. He was rooming there with me. And I used to go there every night on Grandpa Street by him, playing with Tom Anderson upstairs there. And he was playing up there. Sometimes George and Boyd. The cabaret was upstairs. Yeah, upstairs, like the economy hall. Like this hall here at the bandstand, upstairs. Just like people got that stand at the place basically.
